long_biography.plain_text:
Jeffrey Lee Furr earned a Wake Forest law degree and developed a product-liability and mass-tort practice. At King & Spalding, he defended R.J. Reynolds in a tobacco appeal. He also took an entrepreneurial turn in Greensboro, joining Rocco Scarfone in restaurants and live entertainment. Their F&S Restaurant Group arranged a regional Hooters franchise expansion and purchased two existing locations. The restaurant venture was one strand of a wider hospitality partnership rather than a departure from Furr's legal career.

At Cone Denim Entertainment Center, Furr held an ownership interest and the vice-presidency of the venue's operating company. Its rules called for him and Scarfone to discuss major spending and legal decisions together. The precise historical ownership split was disputed in litigation and does not establish either man's share today. Nor is it clear how Furr's earnings from law compare with returns from hospitality, or which of those businesses he still owns. His two business paths remain evident even without a public breakdown of his present assets.
